## Target
`src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py` — **790 LOC** on origin/main against the 800-LOC hard cap (10 lines of headroom).

Ten lines of headroom.

## How to do it
Read the file and derive the seam from the CALL GRAPH — do not take any hint above as the answer.
Extract a cluster of functions that already call each other and that share one concern. The commit
message must NAME the concern boundary you chose and why the call graph supports it.

## Constraints (inherited from the epic — all non-negotiable)
- Split along LOGICAL CONCERNS / ARCHITECTURAL BOUNDARIES, never mechanically to hit a number.
- NEVER raise the limit; `.github/module-size-limit.txt` is locked.
- No resulting file under 100 LOC; target 200-500 LOC each.
- Leave REAL headroom — landing at 798 recreates the problem (that is how Gerrit 1916 failed).
- Behaviour-preserving: existing tests for this area must pass UNMODIFIED. If a test must change,
  the split was not behaviour-preserving — stop and reconsider the seam.
- Serena `find_referencing_symbols` for references, THEN `grep` for each moved symbol AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib). Serena returns EMPTY, not an error, for `Any`
  receivers, so the grep is mandatory.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py` is under the cap with real headroom, and every new file is >= 100 LOC.
- [ ] The split follows an existing call-graph seam; the commit message names the concern boundary.
- [ ] Behaviour unchanged: existing tests covering this area pass UNMODIFIED. BOUNDED EXCEPTION: a
      purely mechanical `<file>:<line>` prose citation inside a test docstring or assertion MESSAGE
      may be repointed when the move shifts the line it names. That is non-behavioural (it changes
      no assertion, no fixture and no import) and is NOT evidence of a bad seam; any change to an
      assertion, fixture, import or expected value IS, and means stop and reconsider the seam.
- [ ] The CI module-size gate passes without touching `.github/module-size-limit.txt`.
- [ ] `make lint` passes.
- [ ] `make typecheck` passes.
- [ ] `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` reports `new=0` and `increased=0`.
- [ ] All references updated — verified by BOTH a semantic reference search AND a string grep.

## Chosen seam (derived from the call graph, 2026-08-19)

**Concern boundary: the step-kind I/O CONTRACT MODEL (declaration + static compatibility) vs the
RUN ENGINE (control flow, expression resolution, dispatch, recording).**

`executor.py` today holds two clusters that share no call edges:

1. *Contract model* - `StepContract`, `STEP_CONTRACTS`, `contract_for`, `input_schema_for`, and the
   3-state shallow structural check (`shallow_contract_check` -> `_schema_is_opaque` /
   `_field_is_opaque` / `_primitive_kinds`). Internal edges only: `input_schema_for` -> `contract_for`
   -> `STEP_CONTRACTS`; `shallow_contract_check` -> its three private helpers. Its consumers are the
   STATIC / edit-time surface: `editor.py`, `editor_contracts.py`, `lint_refs.py`, and the
   interpreter's pre-dispatch input validation.
2. *Run engine* - `new_run_id`, `_capture_nondeterminism`, `RunState`, `RunResult`, the expression
   resolver, `static_order` / `_terminal_step` / `_guard_passes`, `run_workflow`, `_dispatch`,
   `_step_record`, and the snapshot TTL sweep.

The run loop NEVER calls cluster 1. The only edge across the seam is `register_step` writing
`STEP_CONTRACTS`, so cluster 1 moves to a new `step_contracts.py` and `executor.py` imports it -
one direction, no cycle. This is the same pattern the file's two prior splits used
(`recorder.py`, `runners.py`): move the cluster, re-export the public names from `executor` so
every existing import point keeps working.

### Why the OTHER candidate clusters must NOT move
- **Expression resolution** (`resolve_value` / `_resolve_one`) carries the ONE `# read-via:` marked
  line budgeted to `llm/workflow/executor.py` in `tests/scripts/test_llm_seam_clean_heldout.py`
  (`_MARKER_BUDGET`, exact count 1). Moving it turns that budget RED.
- **`run_workflow`** is a live `monkeypatch.setattr` target (`test_code_review_gate_session.py`,
  `test_code_review_provenance.py`, `test_plan_review_cancel.py`), so it stays put.
- **`StepContext` / `StepResult` / `STEP_REGISTRY`** are read as MODULE ATTRIBUTES
  (`_ex.StepContext`, `_ex.STEP_REGISTRY`) across ~50 test modules; they stay, so nothing that binds
  to the module object moves.
- The Burr tripwire (`tests/unit/workflow/test_executor_tripwire.py`) scans `executor.py` +
  `interpreter.py` for banned scheduler/retry imports and for the trigger-list prose. The moved
  cluster contains NO control flow and NO third-party imports, and the docstring stays, so the
  tripwire keeps exactly its intended scope and needs no change.
- `.github/complexity-baseline.json` has ZERO entries keyed to `llm/workflow/executor.py`, so no
  baselined symbol is relocated (verified before choosing the seam).

### Expected shape
`executor.py` ~790 -> ~655 LOC (~145 lines of headroom, below the 720 near-cap warning band);
new `src/rebar/llm/workflow/step_contracts.py` ~190 LOC (over the 100-LOC floor). Moved bodies are
byte-identical apart from imports; the four in-`src` lazy import sites are repointed at the new
module, and `executor` keeps re-exporting `contract_for` / `shallow_contract_check` / `StepContract`
so every existing import (including tests) resolves unchanged.

### The COMPLETE re-export surface (enumerated, one line per moved symbol)
After the move `executor.py` re-binds, at module scope, EVERY cluster-1 symbol that any existing
consumer imports from `rebar.llm.workflow.executor`:

| moved symbol | still imported from `executor` by | executor keeps it because |
|---|---|---|
| `StepContract` | `executor.__all__`; type of `STEP_CONTRACTS` values | `register_step` constructs it |
| `STEP_CONTRACTS` | `tests/unit/workflow/test_contracts.py:18` | `register_step` writes into it |
| `contract_for` | `tests/unit/workflow/test_contracts.py:18`, `tests/interfaces/store/test_workflow_scripted_steps.py:16` | re-export only (already in `__all__`) |
| `shallow_contract_check` | `tests/unit/workflow/test_validation_depth.py:15` | re-export only (already in `__all__`) |

Worked example - `tests/unit/workflow/test_contracts.py:18` reads
`from rebar.llm.workflow.executor import STEP_CONTRACTS, STEP_REGISTRY, contract_for`. After the
move `executor.py` carries
`from .step_contracts import STEP_CONTRACTS, StepContract, contract_for, shallow_contract_check`
at module scope, and `STEP_REGISTRY` never leaves executor, so that exact line resolves unchanged
and the file is not edited. `STEP_CONTRACTS` binds the SAME dict object in both modules, so
`register_step`'s writes are visible through either name.

`input_schema_for` is the one moved symbol with NO import from `executor` anywhere outside `src`
(its only two consumers are the function-local imports in `editor.py:168` and
`interpreter.py:76`), so it is repointed at `step_contracts` rather than re-exported - verified by
`grep -rn 'input_schema_for'` over the whole tree. The private helpers `_schema_is_opaque`,
`_field_is_opaque`, `_primitive_kinds` and `_SHALLOW_COMBINATORS` have no consumer outside the
moved cluster and are not re-exported.

### Verification
Each command below exits non-zero on failure, so a regression is observable without reading output:

- `test "$(wc -l < src/rebar/llm/workflow/executor.py)" -le 720` - executor is under the near-cap
  warning band.
- `test "$(wc -l < src/rebar/llm/workflow/step_contracts.py)" -ge 100` - the new file clears the floor.
- `git diff --exit-code origin/main -- .github/module-size-limit.txt` - the locked limit is untouched.
- `git diff --stat origin/main -- tests/ | grep -qv .` OR, if the only test diff is a repointed
  `<file>:<line>` prose citation, `git diff origin/main -- tests/ | grep -E '^[+-]' | grep -vE
  '^(\+\+\+|---)' | grep -qvE 'executor\.py:[0-9]'` returns non-zero - i.e. no test change other
  than that citation.
- `pytest -m "not integration and not external" tests/unit/workflow tests/unit/workflow/test_contracts.py tests/unit/workflow/test_validation_depth.py tests/unit/workflow/test_executor_tripwire.py tests/unit/test_plan_review_workflow_ops_seam.py tests/scripts/test_llm_seam_clean_heldout.py tests/interfaces/store/test_workflow_scripted_steps.py`
  exits 0.
- `make lint` exits 0 (it runs `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check`, which fails
  the build on any `new>0` or `increased>0`).
- `make typecheck` exits 0.
- `python scripts/check_complexity_baseline.py --check` exits 0.
- Reference sweep: Serena `find_referencing_symbols` on each moved symbol, PLUS
  `grep -rn '<symbol>' --include='*.py' --include='*.md' .` for each name AS A STRING
  (monkeypatch.setattr / getattr / importlib), and the result set must be empty of any site still
  expecting the symbol at its OLD location.
